deities: Mount Kangchenjunga / Khangchendzonga (guardian deity of Sikkim, worshipped at Pang Lhabsol)
Mahakala (dharmapala deity honoured in the 9th-month festival)
festivals: Pang Lhabsol (15th day of the 7th Tibetan month, late August/early September - worship of Mount Kangchenjunga as guardian deity; ends with Kagyed in early December)
Chaam masked dance (15th of the 7th month and 29th of the 10th month)

history.dynasty: Chogyal era - built under the 4th Chogyal Gyurmed Namgyal
history.period: Old monastery: 1730 AD (Iron-Dog year of the 12th Rabjung cycle) per the Sikkim Ecclesiastical Affairs Department; Wikipedia's infobox gives 1768 (verify). Old monastery reconstructed 1975-1981; new Ralong Palchen Choling built 1995.
history.summary: FLAG - CSV TOWN ERROR AND NOT A HINDU TEMPLE: the CSV lists 'Namchi' as the town, but Ralang Monastery stands in Ralang village about 6 km from Ravangla town (South Sikkim) - town corrected to Ravangla. It is a Buddhist monastery of the Kagyu (Kagyupa) sect of Tibetan Buddhism. The old Ralang Gompa - Ralong Karma Rabtenling - is the first monastery of the Kagyupa lineage, built by Sikkim's fourth ruler Chogyal Gyurmed Namgyal in 1730 AD after he returned from a pilgrimage to Tibet where the 12th Karmapa blessed his promise to build it (the older tale crediting the 9th Karmapa's Rabney blessing is flagged as anachronistic by the Sikkim Ecclesiastical Affairs Department, since the 9th Karmapa died in 1603). The old monastery was reconstructed in 1975-1981; the new Ralong Palchen Choling Monastic Institute, a Dharma Chakra centre of the Kagyupa lineage, was built just above it in 1995 by the 12th Gyaltsab Rinpoche in traditional Tibetan architecture, and houses an extensive collection of paintings and thangkas. The monastery hosts the annual Pang Lhabsol festival honouring Mount Khangchendzonga as the guardian deity of Sikkim, with Chaam dances and the Mahakala festival through the year.

name: Ralang Monastery
town_description: Ravangla is a hill town in Namchi district (South Sikkim) at about 2,400 m, a base for the Ralang Monastery (~6 km away), the Buddha Park (Tathagata Tsal) and views of Mt Kanchenjunga, Mt Pandim, Mt Sinialchu and Mt Kabru.
tradition: Buddhism (Tibetan Buddhism, Kagyu order) - NOT a Hindu temple; keep-or-drop decision needed.

travel.airport: Bagdogra Airport, West Bengal, about 125-135 km by road (verify); Pakyong Airport is closer by air distance (verify).
travel.railway: New Jalpaiguri (NJP) Station, West Bengal, about 120-125 km (verify).
travel.road: About 6 km from Ravangla town, reached by taxi; Ravangla is connected by road to Namchi (~25 km), Gangtok (~68 km) and Siliguri.

visitor_information.best_time: April-May for flowers; September to November for clear Kanchenjunga views and the Pang Lhabsol festival season.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Monastery generally open through daylight hours; festival days (Pang Lhabsol, Chaam, Mahakala) draw large gatherings - check locally before visiting.
